detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:03. The shot opens on an insert on the pale sandy road by the sand-pits with the sun going down: a ginger-beer barrow standing derelict on its shafts with a cloth laid over its bottles, black against the burning sky, and beyond it the wheel of a deserted cab with a horse at a nosebag; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is on the sandy road at the height of the barrow's wheel, an arm's length from it, a 50mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT behind the barrow. At the first frame the ginger-beer barrow stands black at the CENTRE and the LEFT half of the frame, two-thirds of the frame's height. The shot is inside this place: Horsell Common with the sun going down in 1894: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze, a stand of young Scots pines, a low raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater a hundred yards off with a black band of heads and shoulders standing along it. The camera tracks sideways to the right, a truck with small amplitude past the barrow's black wheel, keeping the barrow in the left of frame and the cab wheel in the right as the wind comes off the heath, takes the cloth over the bottles and lifts one corner of it clear of the glass, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 the cloth falls back across the necks, the horse at the nosebag paws the sand and the sand drifts along the road, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:03 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
